author: Jack Pilgrim
title: Adam Zouagui set to open season as Kentucky's starting kicker - NewsBreak
text:
By Jack Pilgrim ,
8 hours ago
Kentucky Wildcats kicker Adam Zouagui (88) lines up for a field goal during the first spring game of the Will Stein era on Saturday, April 18, 2026 at Kroger Field in Lexington, Kentucky. Photo by Crawford Ifland, Kentucky Sports Radio/On3 If you’re not familiar with the name Adam Zouagui , you had better learn quickly. That will be Kentucky football’s starting kicker to open the season — and the Will Stein era in Lexington — against Youngstown State on Saturday.
KSR’s Matt Jones is reporting that the 5-foot-11 senior out of Reston, Va., will get the nod when the Penguins come to town.
Zouagui is a transfer from South Florida who also began his career at Davidson, coming in with an all-time hit rate of 11-of-25 on field goals and 99-of-102 on PATs. Last season for the Bulls, he saw action in all 13 games, handling kickoffs with 78 boots for 4,991 yards. That’s an average of 64.0 yards per kickoff with 61 touchbacks.
Now, if you’re concerned about Zouagui hitting just 44 percent of his field goals — including a 4-of-16 finish in 2024, his last time out as a full-time starter — that’s totally fair. Understand, though, that his presence is due to an injury suffered by incumbent starter Jacob Kauwe . The latter will be sidelined for the time being, forcing the Wildcats to rely on his backup until the junior kicker is ready to return to the field.
Kauwe redshirted in 2024 before taking over as Kentucky’s starter in 2025, finishing the year 13-of-17 on field goals and 32-of-32 on PATs, ranking second on the team in scoring behind standout running back Seth McGowan. He was 7-of-9 on field goals longer than 40 yards and 12-of-13 inside 50 yards, adding a 51-yarder against Eastern Michigan for his career-long.
Matt Jones was also the first to report Kauwe’s injury.
Alex Raynor was the starter upon Kauwe’s arrival, going 10-of-11 on field goals and 48-of-49 on PATs in his first season in 2023, followed by a 15-of-16 finish on field goals and 26-of-27 on PATs in 2024. Kauwe did a strong job replacing him last season and is expected to take a bigger step forward in his second year as the full-time kicker.
This setback certainly complicates that, at least initially, and puts quite a bit of pressure on Zouagui to hold down the fort in the meantime. Hopefully Kauwe is back soon, but until then, it’s time to see what Big Z’s got in the tank as a senior.
“It just felt right,” Zouagui told KSR upon committing back in January. “I connected with the staff, loved the culture, and this is a place that expects to win.”
It’s up to him to contribute to those wins in 2026.
